title: Potential evaluation of SULT1A3 as an early diagnostic marker for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a study based on serum proteomics screening and ELISA validation.
summary: The publisher version and the first Research Square version agree on the serum and plasma proteomics screen, the RF-RFE prioritization of SULT1A3 and the independent ELISA cohorts. The work supports SULT1A3 as a candidate nasopharyngeal carcinoma marker rather than a clinically ready screening test, and the cohorts are geographically limited.
ai_technology: Random forest with recursive feature elimination prioritizes protein candidates from 15 early NPC and 15 VCA-IgA-positive control samples.

evidence.tested: ELISA validation reports SULT1A3 AUC .787 in n=80 and AUC .826 and .796 in separate cohorts n=196 and n=150, with sensitivities/specificities around 77–79%; LTA4H/FGL1 weaker.
evidence.unknown: Multistage independent ELISA cohorts directly test the candidate; modest discrimination and single-region cohorts require further multicenter validation.
